Circuit-level analyses have since traced complete computational subgraphs for tasks such as indirect object identification~\cite{wang2023_ioi} and greater-than comparison~\cite{conmy2023}.
Meng et al.~\cite{meng2022_rome} developed causal tracing to locate factual associations in specific MLP layers, and Belrose et al.~\cite{belrose2023_tunedlens} introduced the tuned lens for tracking per-layer prediction evolution through learned projections.
In parallel, attention probing studies have shown that individual heads encode syntactic relations~\cite{clark2019}, capture positional and structural patterns at different depths~\cite{vig2019}, and that a small subset of specialized heads accounts for most model performance~\cite{voita2019}.
Our Layer-1 attention head analysis extends this tradition to the VLA domain; unlike knowledge editing or prediction lens approaches, we use functional ablation to study task-specific routing and find that 24 of 32 heads become instruction-dominant after fine-tuning.
